Topics · One God, one message

Does any race or nation stand higher with God?

One measure of honour no one can inherit or see, the first to say "I am better", and a caution to believers.

Part 1 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَـٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous[1521] of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

Translator's notes

[1521] Literally, "he who has the most taqwā," i.e., consciousness and fear of Allāh, piety and righteousness.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:13

Translation

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,

Acts · 17:26

World English Bible

For one people to stand above another, you need a measure. The usual ones are three: what you were born with, what you own, and what you are. This verse removes the first two with a single word, the most mindful of God. That cannot be inherited, bought, or read from skin. Then it closes the door on every claimant: the knowledge of it belongs to God. No one can measure it, and no one can carry it as a banner.

A question for you

If someone asked what you are truly proud of, where would most of it come from?

If you sayMy family and people
ThenLove of your own is a good thing, and the verse does not forbid it. It separates loving what you were born into from making it the measure of a person's worth.
If you sayWhat I worked for
ThenThat is nearer to what the verse weighs, and it keeps a finer question: who knows what is in the heart as you work?
If you sayI am not sure
ThenAn honest answer, and a good place to walk the rest of this from.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنَـٰكُمْ ثُمَّ صَوَّرْنَـٰكُمْ ثُمَّ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسْجُدُوا۟ لِـَٔادَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّـٰجِدِينَ١١ قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ ۖ قَالَ أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍ١٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have certainly created you, [O mankind], and given you [human] form. Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"; so they prostrated, except for Iblees.[364] He was not of those who prostrated. [Allāh] said, "What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?" [Satan] said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay [i.e., earth]."

Translator's notes

[364] Satan. See footnote to 2:34.

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:11-12

One of the oldest arguments for rank by origin is recorded here: I am better than him, because of what I was made from. Notice how it is built. The speaker does not claim to be more obedient, truthful or kind. He argues from what he was made of. Every claim of racial rank says the same: my worth is in my material. The Quran places this argument in the mouth of the one who refused, so it is worth noticing whenever we catch ourselves using it.

A question for you

What changed when the answer was about substance, not about the deed?

If you sayIt could no longer be changed
ThenA deed can be repaired; a substance cannot. That is why this pride closes the way back on its owner first of all.
If you sayHe excused himself from the question
ThenSo substance served as an excuse. You may ask how many of our judgments of people work the same way.
If you sayNothing changed
ThenPerhaps. Compare then the one who says "I was wrong" with the one who says "I am better", and see which of them still has a road.

Part 3 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُونُوا۟ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُمْ وَلَا نِسَآءٌ مِّن نِّسَآءٍ عَسَىٰٓ أَن يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِّنْهُنَّ ۖ وَلَا تَلْمِزُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَكُمْ وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا۟ بِٱلْأَلْقَـٰبِ ۖ بِئْسَ ٱلِٱسْمُ ٱلْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ ٱلْإِيمَـٰنِ ۚ وَمَن لَّمْ يَتُبْ فَأُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name [i.e., mention] of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:11

Translation

Don’t laugh a man to scorn when he is in the bitterness of his soul, for there is one who humbles and exalts.

Original · Ancient Greek

Μὴ καταγέλα ἄνθρωπον ὄντα ἐν πικρίᾳ ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ, ἔστι γὰρ ὁ ταπεινῶν καὶ ἀνυψῶν.

Sirach · 7:11

World English Bible

A reader may assume this is meant for someone else. So look at this verse. It does not address outsiders. It speaks to believers themselves, face to face: let no people mock another people, for those may be better than they are. The argument is precise. Since you do not hold God's balance, you cannot rule that anyone is beneath you. A community of faith is not excused from the rule; it is the first to be told it.

A question for you

Who are the people your own group finds it easy to laugh at?

The same in the other books

Translation

Peter opened his mouth and said, “Truly I perceive that God doesn’t show favoritism; but in every nation he who fears him and works righteousness is acceptable to him.

Acts · 10:34-35
